### Seneca on time

Seneca (c. 4 BCE–65 CE) approaches time within Stoicism. Philosophy is therapy for destructive passions; anger especially must be starved before it hardens into cruelty. Time is our scarcest good; busyness without reflection wastes life. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets time most directly—useful for searches such as “seneca quotes on time.”

### How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the [Seneca thinker page](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) for biography and to the [time theme](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/time) for other voices on the same question.
